subject: Unexpected 5xx/429 surge - customer-side reattempt loop (VoltEdge)
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <ops@voltedge.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2026 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Spike in 5xx/429 and client timeouts - saw surge at 08:50 PT

Hi Kimberly,

We're seeing a large spike of 5xx and 429 responses from Redwood starting around 08:50 PT this morning. Our service is timing out on a bunch of inference calls and we're getting paged. I attached a short trace and a screenshot of the headers we capture. This started shortly after we rolled SDK v2.1.0 to a subset of clients (about 25% traffic).

Key observations:
- 429 and 5xx rate jumped to ~15% for a 20 minute window
- Client timeouts increased to 600ms -> 2s+
- We rolled the SDK at 08:40 PT; we reverted the rollout at 09:05 PT but issues persisted for ~30 mins after

Can you confirm if this is on your side, or if the SDK could be aggressively reattempting and amplifying load? We need an urgent mitigation while we investigate.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
VP, Platform Operations
VoltEdge
Attachments: request-trace-20261201.json, screenshot-client-headers.png

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: infra-oncall@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2026 09:33:00 -08:00
Subject: ACTION: Apply temporary per-key smoothing + throttle for VoltEdge (VOLT-2026-EXP)

Infra team — VoltEdge is experiencing a rapid 5xx/429 spike that lines up with a customer SDK rollout. Attachments from customer indicate repeated identical request patterns and no exponential backoff. Please: 
1) Apply a short-term token-bucket smoothing on their API key to cap burst concurrency to 50 rps for the next 30 minutes.
2) Enable our client-fallback routing to lower-cost model variant to reduce pressure.
3) Share traces and top-attempting IPs back to me and kimberly.

This is an elevated customer incident; we're aiming to stabilize within 30 minutes.

-Aditya
From: infra-oncall@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2026 09:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: ACTION: Apply temporary per-key smoothing + throttle for VoltEdge (VOLT-2026-EXP)

On Wed, Dec 1, 2026 at 09:33 AM aditya_rao@redwood.ai wrote:
> Infra team — VoltEdge is experiencing a rapid 5xx/429 spike that lines up with a customer SDK rollout...

We applied a 50rps token-bucket cap and enabled smoothing for VoltEdge API key at 09:39 PT. We also pushed a temporary rate-limiter that applies random jitter to retry responses for 10 minutes to break synchronization. Initial telemetry shows 5xx/429 rate dropped from 14.8% to 2.1% within 5 minutes and latency tail improved. Pushing full traces to Drive.

Attachments: voltedge_traces_20261201.zip

- oncall infra
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, Marta Ruiz <ops@voltedge.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Root-cause hypothesis and recommended next steps

Marta / team — thanks for the trace. Preliminary analysis: the client traces show deterministic immediate retries with a fixed 200ms interval and no jitter or exponential backoff. With a subset rollout at 25% and many clients concurrently failing, that pattern creates a classic amplification loop. Key notes: 
- SDK v2.1.0 appears to set maxAttempts=6 with constant 200ms sleep and jitter disabled by default.
- When upstream returns 429/5xx, many clients reissued simultaneous attempts, multiplying load.

Recommended remediation: 
1) We recommend that VoltEdge rollback SDK 2.1.0 to 2.0.x for the remainder of the rollout until a backoff fix is available.
2) Apply jittered exponential backoff in the SDK (base 100-200ms, multiplier 2x, jitter 10-30%).
3) Redwood will publish a short KB and a preflight checklist for SDK rollouts that includes rate-limiting and backoff validation.

We'll coordinate a shared postmortem after metrics settle. Happy to jump on a call to walk through traces.

— Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marta Ruiz <ops@voltedge.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@voltedge.com
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2026 11:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 and client timeouts - customer rollout correlation

Thanks, Priyom and team. We confirmed in our rollout that the new SDK enabled a fixed retry without jitter (bad call on our side). We started a rollback at 09:05 PT; the infra mitigations you applied helped with the tail but we still saw residual load until ~10:30.

Action items from VoltEdge:
- Full rollback to 2.0.7 completed at 11:00 PT.
- Ship a patched SDK with exponential backoff + jitter by Friday (2026-12-03).
- We'd like Redwood to provide a KB and a sample test harness we can run before future rollouts.

Appreciate the quick response — this prevented a larger outage for our customers.

Marta
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Exec summary for leadership — VoltEdge 429/5xx surge (postmortem pending)

Team — quick exec note to capture outcome and follow-ups for leadership and CSM: 

Summary: VoltEdge experienced an elevated 5xx/429 rate following SDK v2.1.0 rollout that removed jittered exponential backoff, causing synchronized client retries and an amplification loop. Redwood applied short-term mitigations (per-key token-bucket, jitter injection, fallback routing) which reduced 5xx/429 from ~15% to ~2% within minutes. VoltEdge rolled back the SDK; final stability observed by 10:30 PT on 2026-12-01.

Impact: Customer-facing latency and increased error rate; no revenue loss expected; potential upsell risk if trust not rebuilt.

Follow-ups: 
- Priyom to draft a public KB and a preflight harness for client SDK rollouts (ETA: 2026-12-07).
- Aditya / Kimberly to propose a joint postmortem on 12/08 and include VoltEdge on the readout.
- Product to consider a server-side safeguard change: enforce per-key burst caps and a “retry pattern” detector that can auto-slow keys showing synchronous attempts (Product sync 12/10).

I'll package this into the formal incident postmortem and share in Drive. Thanks all for the rapid response.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
